title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as companies pivot towards AI and on-orbit computing, while nations like China ramp up their rocket development. Meanwhile, the U.S. grapples with the need for a coherent response strategy to potential threats in space.

themes.title: AI in Earth Observation
themes.body: Loft Orbital's upcoming tests of AI models on spacecraft signal a shift towards more intelligent data processing in Earth observation. This could enhance the speed and accuracy of satellite data analysis, making it more valuable for various applications.

themes.title: Resilience Funding Boost
themes.body: The recent $1.4 billion addition to the FY27 budget for space resilience reflects a growing recognition of the need to fortify U.S. capabilities in the face of emerging threats. This funding could catalyze innovations in satellite technology and defensive measures.

themes.title: International Rocket Developments
themes.body: China's apparent progress on 7-meter-diameter reusable rockets adds another layer of complexity to the global space race. As nations ramp up their capabilities, the balance of power in space is likely to shift, prompting strategic recalibrations.

themes.title: Defense-Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The potential opening of the defense-tech IPO window suggests that investors are increasingly interested in the intersection of technology and national security. This could lead to a wave of new entrants in the space sector, reshaping the competitive landscape.
